findings.title: --apply-canon --adopt-commits 同時指定の composability テストが存在しない

findings.title: null runStore → PrepareError(1) のテストケースが欠落している

observations.title: apply-canon の null runStore サイレントスキップは本 change 外の既存挙動
observations.rationale: apply-canon gate では runStore が null の場合 persist が例外なしにスキップされる（split-brain guard も発動しない）。adopt-commits の T-04 では null runStore を明示的に PrepareError(1) とする設計が求められており、既存 apply-canon より正しい。本 change の導入で非対称が生じるが、apply-canon 側の修正は今回のスコープ外。

message: verification iteration 1 completed with verdict: passed

findings.title: TC-005 test 2 exercises the wrong failure mode
findings.rationale: The second TC-005 test uses `mockRejectedValue` to reject ALL persist calls. Because the initial state-transition persist (resume.ts ~248) fires first, prepare() throws there — not at the adoption persist. The assertion `threw === true` passes but for the wrong reason. TC-005 test 1 (with `persistCallCount >= 2`) correctly targets the adoption persist failure and provides the real coverage for this AC. Test 2 is misleadingly labelled and would not catch a bug where the adoption persist guard was silently removed while the state-transition guard remained.

findings.title: Escalation message uses stderrWrite only; T-04 spec requires logError (or logError summary + stderrWrite)
findings.rationale: T-04 specifies `logError(msg)` or `logError` a summary + `stderrWrite(msg)`. The implementation calls only `stderrWrite(msg)` for the escalation. The apply-canon gate (resume.ts ~343-344) follows the summary+hint pattern with logError then stderrWrite. Diverging from that pattern means if log-level filtering or capture is applied to stderrWrite in future, the escalation could be suppressed. Tests pass today because they check both channels.

observations.title: No-worktree mode: operator commits bypass the adopt gate (documented scope gap)
observations.rationale: The adopt gate is inside `if (resolvedWorktreePath !== null)`, mirroring the apply-canon gate. A --no-worktree resume carrying an unknown committed OID bypasses the gate and hits the in-pipeline egress check after a full step runs. Design D3 explicitly documents this as a scoped limitation and the improved egressUnknownCommitError message (D6) partially mitigates it. No action needed.

findings.title: hand-push convention コメントが新挙動（--adopt-commits）と矛盾したまま未更新

findings.title: --adopt-commits が no-worktree / worktree 非解決時に警告なく無視される
findings.rationale: resolvedWorktreePath === null のとき adopt gate ブロック全体がスキップされる。変更していない else if (this.options.applyCanon) ブランチ（resume.ts:411-414）は --apply-canon が無効になるとき警告を出すが、--adopt-commits に対応する警告は追加されていない。operator が EGRESS_UNKNOWN_COMMIT メッセージ（新三択）の option 1 を見て --no-worktree --adopt-commits を試みると警告なしに無視され、再び in-pipeline で halt する。design.md Risks は「in-pipeline egress check が three-option message を持つ」とするが runtime 警告は実装されていない。

findings.title: adopt gate の fail-closed halt が logError を経由せず apply-canon gate の出力パターンと非対称
findings.rationale: 変更していない apply-canon gate（resume.ts:341-346）は logError(要約) + stderrWrite(hint) のパターンを確立している。新 adopt gate（resume.ts:387-391）は stderrWrite(full message) のみで logError を経由しない。TC-003 は logError と stderrWrite の和集合に assertion を書くため現状でも pass するが、ログアグリゲーターが [ERROR] プレフィックスでフィルタする場合や将来 stderrWrite に logLevel フィルタが適用された場合に escalation が見えなくなるリスクがある。

observations.title: TC-005 テスト 2 が adopt persist ではなく running 遷移 persist の失敗を踏んでいる

observations.title: adopt gate halt 後の running/dead 状態は stale-detection で正常回復することを確認

findings.title: TC-005 test 2 still rejects ALL persist calls — adoption persist guard is not specifically exercised
findings.rationale: TC-005 test 2 uses `vi.mocked(MOCK_STORE.persist).mockRejectedValue(new Error('persist failed'))` which rejects every persist call. The initial state-transition persist at resume.ts:248 fires first and throws PrepareError(1, 'Failed to update state'), so `threw === true` passes for the wrong reason. If the adoption persist guard were silently removed while the state-transition guard remained, this test would still pass. TC-005 test 1 (persistCallCount >= 2) correctly targets the adoption persist and provides the real coverage, but test 2 remains misleadingly labelled and adds no discriminating value.

findings.title: Adopt gate escalation calls only stderrWrite; no logError call (findings #4 and #7 both unresolved)
findings.rationale: resume.ts:386-390 calls stderrWrite(msg) but not logError for the adopt gate halt. The apply-canon gate at resume.ts:343-344 follows logError(summary) + stderrWrite(hint). T-04 spec requires logError or logError-summary+stderrWrite. TC-003 tests use a union check ([...logErrorCalls, ...stderrCalls]) so they pass today with stderrWrite alone. A log-level filter or [ERROR]-prefix aggregator would suppress the escalation message entirely. Both findings #4 and #7 from the ledger describe the same defect at the same line.

findings.title: Comment still says 'operator hand-commits are hand-pushed' — contradicts --adopt-commits
findings.rationale: commit-push.ts:388-389 still reads 'operator hand-commits are hand-pushed' as the assumed path for pre-existing operator commits to leave the publish range. --adopt-commits is a second path where commits remain local but are registered in the ledger. The comment was not updated, creating a design.md D2 contradiction in the code. A future developer reading this comment could incorrectly treat --adopt-commits as redundant and remove it.

findings.title: --adopt-commits is silently ignored when resolvedWorktreePath is null; no warning added
findings.rationale: resume.ts:411-413 warns when --apply-canon is given without a worktree, but no corresponding warning was added for --adopt-commits. When resolvedWorktreePath === null the entire adopt gate block is skipped silently. An operator who follows the three-option EGRESS_UNKNOWN_COMMIT message (option 1: use --adopt-commits) and runs with --no-worktree --adopt-commits will see a silent no-op and hit the same halt at the next step's egress check.

observations.title: TC-013: --apply-canon + --adopt-commits composability test fully added
observations.rationale: TC-013 (lines 899-999) adds four assertions covering the D4 composability claim: prepare() resolves with both flags, persisted state contains both OIDs, apply-canon OID appears exactly once (not re-adopted), and detectUnadoptedCommits receives the post-apply-canon ledger. This was the MEDIUM ledger finding and is confirmed fixed.

observations.title: TC-011: null runStore → PrepareError(1) test confirmed present
observations.rationale: TC-011 (lines 775-826) tests both that prepare() throws exitCode=1 when resolveStateStoreByJobId returns null with adoptCommits:true, and that it is fail-closed (not a silent no-op). The null runStore guard at resume.ts:375-378 is present and exercised.
